Class Mechanism

java.lang.Object
frc.spectrumLib.mechanism.Mechanism
All Implemented Interfaces:
Subsystem
Direct Known Subclasses:
FuelIntake, Hood, IndexerBed, IndexerTower, IntakeExtension, IntakeExtension.IntakeExtensionRight, Launcher
public abstract class Mechanism extends Object implements Subsystem
Abstract base class representing a CTRE TalonFX-driven robot mechanism with common control modes, telemetry, and convenience Command factories.

This class centralizes:

  • Motor creation/configuration (leader + optional followers) via the provided Mechanism.Config
  • Cached sensor readings (position, velocity, voltage, current) for efficient access
  • Common unit conversions (rotations/percent/degrees; RPS/RPM)
  • Standard closed-loop and open-loop control helpers (Motion Magic, velocity, voltage, percent, torque current)
  • Convenience Trigger factories (at/above/below thresholds)
  • Basic periodic current reporting to a battery/current logger

Attachment semantics

If Mechanism.Config.isAttached() is false, the mechanism will not attempt to construct or command hardware and will return safe default sensor values (typically 0).

Target tracking

The target field tracks the last commanded closed-loop setpoint sent by this class. It is used by helper triggers such as atTargetPosition(...).

Tracking stop

A mechanism whose config sets a tracking tolerance (Mechanism.Config.configPositionTrackingStop(double, double, boolean), Mechanism.Config.configVelocityTrackingStop(double, double, boolean)) logs TrackingError and TrackingFault under Mechanisms/<name>/. With Mechanism.Config.isTrackingStopEnabled() it also latches to neutral on a fault, until disabled or clearTrackingStop(). See TrackingStop.

Extending

Concrete mechanisms should provide a Mechanism.Config describing motor IDs, Talon configuration, follower configuration, and mechanism-specific min/max rotation bounds as needed.

Note: This class assumes CTRE Phoenix 6 units (rotations, rotations/sec, etc.) and uses Config.talonConfig.Feedback.SensorToMechanismRatio as the mechanism gearing ratio.

    • refreshSignalsOncePerLoop

      protected void refreshSignalsOncePerLoop()
      Refreshes every status signal this mechanism reads, once per robot loop, in one Phoenix call.

      Every Phoenix getter such as motor.getStatorCurrent() defaults to refreshing its signal, which is a JNI call each. With eight signals per mechanism read once or more a loop that was over a hundred JNI calls per loop across the robot. CTRE's recommendation is one refreshAll for the lot, which is what this does; every read in the same loop then sees the same sample, which is the behaviour the per-value caches used to provide.

    • clampToSoftLimits

      public double clampToSoftLimits(double rotations)
      The nearest position the motor can reach under the soft limits it booted with (each one only while enabled). Soft-limit params apply at boot only, so these are the motor's limits even after a params edit.
      Parameters:

      Returns:

    • hasSoftLimits

      public boolean hasSoftLimits()
      The leader's position bounds its travel, so a reboot that restarts it matters.
      Returns:

    • isPositionLost

      public boolean isPositionLost()
      The leader rebooted since this mechanism last set its position, so the position, the soft limits and any position setpoint are measured from a zero the reboot erased. Until a position write (homing) clears it, every soft-limited output is replaced by neutral. Only soft-limited mechanisms lose their position this way.
      Returns:
      true while the position cannot be trusted

    • isPositionWritePending

      public boolean isPositionWritePending()
      A position write (setMotorPosition(DoubleSupplier)) went out and the readings do not show it yet, so they are still measured from the old zero. Setpoints are held meanwhile; logic that reads the position as homed should wait too. Usually a loop or two.
      Returns:
      true until the readings show the written position

    • motorResetThisLoop

      protected boolean motorResetThisLoop()
      The leader's reset input this loop, after refreshing it. A mechanism that homes itself restarts its homing on this.
      Returns:
      true on the loop a reboot is seen

    • isTrackingStopped

      public boolean isTrackingStopped()
      This mechanism stayed out of tolerance of its goal past the debounce and is held in neutral (brake or coast per its config) until the robot is disabled or clearTrackingStop(). A re-home does not release it: homing takes a stall for the stop, so a jammed mechanism would zero itself at the jam.
      Returns:
      true while the tracking stop holds the mechanism

    • clearTrackingStop

      public void clearTrackingStop()
      The operator's override: releases the tracking stop. It latches again if still stuck.

      Refreshes the motor inputs for this loop. Called from periodic() so the inputs are recorded every loop even when nothing reads them; subclasses that override periodic() get the same from their first getter call.
